preview: An interview experience at Morgan Stanley consisting of an online test, a technical round, an HR round, and a final round with the Executive Director.
content:
Morgan Stanley Interview Experience

Round 1: Online Test

The first round contained 3 modules. One was debugging, one quantitative aptitude, and one coding round. We had a total of 100 minutes, split into 20, 20 and 60 for each module respectively. Debugging and Aptitude had 7 and 10 questions respectively. Coding had 3 problems, of which I solved 1 completely and 1 partially.

Round 2: Technical Round

6 people were shortlisted for this round based on the online test. This was a technical round. It started with tell me about yourself. Then I was given certain problems based on data structures and asked to solve them.

Questions:
1. Suppose there is a table you want to store as follows:
Year
City
Avg Temperature
2017
Mumbai
28
2017
Chennai
40
2018
Mumbai
32
2019
Mumbai
35

Implement a data structure that gives average temperate of a city (over all the years)

Eg. If city = Mumbai, return (28+32+35)/3
• I said a map would be good such that you map a pair of strings to a temperature. I was asked to implement code for getting average temperature by city.
• I was then asked many questions based on maps, multimaps, their advantages & disadvantages, why is a map better than a hash, what’s the difference and so on.
• Then I was asked to implement a class map such that the lookup time in that was O(1) (basically using hashing). Then I was asked how would I solve the problem of collision in the map that I implemented. I gave a linear probing solution. I was asked to implement the code at each and every step.

2. Given a sparse matrix give the best way to store it in memory (the size of the matrix is not given to you)
I gave list of lists solution. They were satisfied with it.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sparse-matrix-representation/

https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sparse-matrix-representations-using-list-lists-dictionary-keys/

3. Print boundary traversal of binary tree
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/boundary-traversal-of-binary-tree/

I first gave a recursive solution.
I was then asked to implement a non-recursive solution. I gave one and they were satisfied.

They then asked me what’s the difference between a process and a thread and whether I knew any scheduling algorithms. I said I don’t know as it has not been taught to us yet. They didn’t ask further questions on that. (Be honest about anything you don’t know)

Last part of this round was based on SQL joins, queries.

Round 3: HR Round

This round was a profile fitness round. I was given many situations and asked how I would approach them. I was also asked a bit about my roles in the technical fest, how I was part of it and some situations too.

Round 4:

This round was with the Executive Director. He first asked me to design a coffee shop. And then he asked me 2 puzzles.

Also, I was asked to give a brief description of the work I did during my previous internship and about my projects in each round. (all of these were mentioned in my resume)

Finally, 3 of us were selected.
